bug_semantics: With a finite memoryLimit and attacker-controlled template content, the replace filter accounts only for input-sized data before executing str.split(pattern).join(replacement). If a short pattern occurs many times and replacement is long, the output is approximately occurrence_count * replacement.length while Limiter.use() sees only str.length (at introduction, later str.length + pattern.length + replacement.length). Because src/util/limiter.ts is only an accumulator checked at use() time and performs no post-allocation validation, the rendered string can exceed the configured limit by orders of magnitude and exhaust process memory.
flaw_origin: The reconstructable PR member 4395697adb63675d75e2db54bea5b4b4b00671dc first introduced memoryLimit and coupled src/filters/string.ts replace to it, but charged only str.length before the pre-existing split/join expansion. The later 94440a065333c78dee461af0049dd712c35f9e45 changed that charge to the sum of the three inputs, which is the exact expression quoted by the advisory, but preserved rather than introduced the causal input-accounting flaw.

The split/join replace implementation predates memoryLimit, so its ability to allocate a large output was not yet a bypass of that protection. PR 715 introduced the protection in a squash. Decomposing its two public member commits is required: 68142d2377b799bcb2c30c959389e3bd4956dc23 is unrelated MapFS work, while its child 4395697adb63675d75e2db54bea5b4b4b00671dc adds the limiter and charges replace only by input string length. The direct parent therefore lacks the vulnerable limiter coupling, and 4395697adb63675d75e2db54bea5b4b4b00671dc is the smallest reconstructed causal BIC rather than landed squash e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2. Commit 94440a065333c78dee461af0049dd712c35f9e45 later made input accounting stricter but still ignored occurrence multiplication, so it is not the origin. Fix abc058be0f33d6372cd2216f4945183167abeb25 splits once, computes exact outputSize as str.length + (parts.length - 1) * (replacement.length - pattern.length), charges that amount, and joins the same parts. The feature first shipped in v10.15.0, remained flawed through v10.25.2, and the direct fix first appears in v10.25.3. Finally, only the decomposed BIC commit object is used for attribution: it is authored and committed by Yang Jun and contains no AI or bot marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
